memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When you have finished setting aside a tenth of all your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, you shall give it to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow, so that they may eat in your towns and be satisfied." — Deut 26:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Every third year, Israel set aside a special tithe — not for the temple, not for a festival, but for the people most likely to be forgotten. The Levite with no inheritance, the foreigner far from home, the fatherless child, the widow with no husband to provide. God built care for the vulnerable right into the rhythm of His people's life.

This tells us something wonderful about God's heart. He notices the ones the world overlooks. The lonely, the poor, the outsider, the grieving — they are not off God's radar. In fact, He commands His people to make sure they "eat and be satisfied." Their satisfaction mattered to God.

We live under a different covenant, so this is not a rule about a three-year tithe cycle for us. But the character of God behind it never changes. He still has a tender heart toward the vulnerable, and He still calls His people to open their hands to them. The New Testament says pure religion includes caring for orphans and widows (Jas 1:27).

Look around you. Who is the "widow," the "foreigner," the forgotten one in your world? God may be inviting you to be the answer to their need, reflecting His own generous heart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who are the "forgotten ones" in my community that God may want me to notice?
2. Am I as concerned about the vulnerable as God is?
3. What is one practical way I can help someone in need this month?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Compassionate Father, You see and care for the forgotten. Give me Your eyes for the vulnerable around me, and Your open hands to help. Amen.
